entries.subject: Beddingfield et al. 2025 medial-groove/geology work, followed by Tonoian et al. structural mapping
entries.finding: Unresolved complementary interpretive candidate. The examined releases describe geological figures and continued structural mapping, but did not establish a downloadable georeferenced unit raster/vector closure suitable for this renderer. No geological lens is claimed.

entries.subject: USGS Ariel Voyager control networks
entries.finding: The inspected release republishes RAND and Jigsaw control solutions and is retained as registration support. It is not an additional image or measured-scalar lens.

entries.subject: Monochrome display-range comparison
entries.finding: The existing visual trial compared upper bounds of 2400, 3000 and 3600 DN and selected 3000 DN. This is a display-contrast choice applied to the retained numeric mosaic, not an albedo calibration.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet colour frames
entries.finding: 9 GEOMED frames in 3 complete sets (1.3 to 19.8 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color lens. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (1.0, 1.05); the archive calibration gives 0.873 and 0.972. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Helfenstein, Veverka and Thomas (1988) fitted Hapke models to Voyager whole-disc photometry of the five large Uranian moons. Only the abstract could be read (single-scattering albedo from 0.3 for Umbriel to 0.7 for Ariel, g near -0.3), and a whole-disc fit states no emission range. Schenk's 2020 mosaic history names ISIS photomet without its parameter file. Ariel keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved law for Ariel with its fitted emission range is read in the paper, or the photometric parameter file of Schenk's mosaic is released.

entries.subject: Native calibrated LORRI CA06 exposure of 1 January 2019
entries.finding: The opening view paints the native calibrated photograph at about 33 m per native pixel: every nonzero quality flag, nonfinite value and negative uncertainty is rejected, absolute-calibration keywords do not convert the stored DN to I/F, and a common linear grayscale stretch preserves the photographed illumination, so the relative DN/s display is not a measured albedo map and retains detector noise and acquisition shadows.

entries.subject: MVIC CA05 colour cube
entries.finding: The MVIC lens uses the provider-aligned, blur-matched cube at 340 m per native pixel: NIR, red and blue share one zero-based 0-0.17 display scale followed by the shared IEC sRGB transfer, the original PDS label validates band order, wavelengths and data-number units, and no separate channel stretch or photometric correction changes their ratios, so this fixes screen encoding without reconstructing natural colour or claiming absolute reflectance.

entries.subject: Porter (2024) fitted LORRI single-scattering albedo
entries.finding: Modeled albedo is the fitted scalar model stretched to grayscale over 0.03-0.08, retaining the release's uniform baseline unchanged: Porter fitted 30 approach images weighted by original resolution, the decoded release spans 0.031881675 to 0.079999998 entirely inside that range, and the lower approximate value discussed in the paper is not substituted for the actual release.

entries.subject: Porter released shape mesh
entries.finding: All four views use a 1,000-triangle reduction of the released 40,960-face, two-lobed mesh of 20,484 vertices; preparation simplifies the full source connectivity without constructing a joining neck or using centre-ray reconstruction.

entries.subject: Fitted encounter attitudes and the held-out LORRI validation exposure
entries.finding: Spin phase and two image-pointing offsets were fitted against the lit source-mesh limb with alternating edge samples withheld, keeping the original WCS scale, TAN-SIP distortion, observer range and Sun vector; CA05 and CA06 phases differ by 4.56 degrees over 741 seconds against the approximately 4.65 degrees implied by the published period, and a separate exposure one second later, reserved for validation and never painted, has 2.29 px RMS residual on its held-out lit edges, which measures image-to-shape alignment rather than absolute terrain accuracy.

entries.subject: Image-space similarity registering MVIC to CA05 LORRI
entries.finding: An image-space similarity registers the cube to the contemporaneous LORRI exposure with held-out limb distances of 2.12 resampled pixels RMS, or 0.71 native MVIC pixels, retaining the LORRI SIP distortion and not reusing the cube label's older body-fixed geometry fields; it approximates the small geometry changes during the TDI scan and is not a new geometric backplane product.

entries.subject: Independent Astropy and NumPy decoding of the native products
entries.finding: The pinned Astropy 8.0.1 and NumPy 2.5.3 fixture covers all three FITS HDUs of both registration images and the four-band cube, comparing native pixels, quality decisions and 50 TAN-SIP camera projections, with both million-pixel detector quality masks matching Astropy's accepted-pixel counts; 24 independent PNG anchors reproduce FITS values within 3e-6 albedo despite the PDS PNG and raw FITS arrays having opposite row order.

entries.subject: Observation-coverage mask for the albedo release
entries.finding: The albedo release has no explicit observational coverage mask and its broad uniform baseline is retained source fill rather than evidence of measured global albedo; no confidence mask is invented from that fill and the default view states the limitation beside the active dataset.
entries.revisitWhen: The archive publishes an observation-coverage or confidence mask for the fitted albedo.

entries.subject: Disagreeing pole and period metadata
entries.finding: The bundled Porter paper and the PDS XML disagree on the pole, and the XML calls a sub-day period an orbital period: the revised paper pole at right ascension 319.37 degrees and declination -25.588 degrees is used with an arbitrary reference meridian, Buie et al. (2020) gives 15.9380 +/-0.0005 h against the archive's 0.6632553 days, the panel reports only about 15.9 hours and no precision spin rate is installed.
entries.revisitWhen: The archive metadata is corrected, or a publication settles the pole and rotation period.

entries.subject: Shape of the unobserved northern side
entries.finding: The photographs cover part of the encounter-facing surface and the grid marks unseen, grazing or rejected coverage; the unseen northern shape remains a source model estimate, shared-edge triangle ties limit exact texture correspondence and no local terrain accuracy is inferred.
entries.revisitWhen: New observations or a revised mesh constrain the unobserved side.

entries.subject: 2023 geophysics archive CA06_STACK_NORMALREFLECTANCE
entries.finding: The archive releases nine LORRI images transformed into the CA06 geometry with signed I/F samples and anomalously bright limb artefacts; because Porter 2024 revises the pole and recentres the body, the old image would need a controlled registration to this exact mesh, so the new photographic views do not promote it to a registered map.
entries.revisitWhen: A controlled registration of the normalized stack to the Porter 2024 mesh is performed.

entries.subject: Companion hemispherical-albedo raster and archive thermal products
entries.finding: The hemispherical-albedo raster differs from the selected product only by a multiplicative factor and would add no independent terrain detail, and the archive's thermal products are simulations on an older mesh rather than measured temperature images.
entries.revisitWhen: A thermal or albedo product is released that carries independent measured detail on the current mesh.

entries.subject: Surface spectra and unresolved observations as textures
entries.finding: The source survey records that surface spectra and unresolved observations are not reconstructed surface textures.
entries.revisitWhen: A resolved spectral map registered to this mesh is released.

entries.subject: Registration verdict for the two photographic lenses
entries.finding: The prepared registration report records one frame per lens with no reference observation, so LORRI is unscored and MVIC has a 3.00-degree limb RMS, and both lenses end with no verdict.
entries.revisitWhen: A second frame or a reference observation lets the registration stage reach a verdict.

entries.subject: USGS global photographic mosaic
entries.finding: The 15,138 × 7,569 USGS Voyager/Galileo global mosaic supplies Monochrome on its roughly 1 km grid. Native detail ranges from 400 m to 60 km; the published Lunar-Lambert/overlap correction and exact-zero no-data are retained.

entries.subject: NASA/JPL/DLR PIA03456 via the official USGS RGBA release
entries.finding: The original 646 × 653 published plate supplies Galileo color, registered to the controlled monochrome mosaic using a frozen perspective camera and independent landmarks/quadrants. The 65° emission limit retains 28.735% of the sphere. These are processed display colors, not calibrated reflectance or natural-color reconstruction.

entries.subject: Galileo NIMS G8CNADLIND01A and G8CNGLOBAL02A
entries.finding: The registered Minnaert-corrected CIOF products supply partial Infrared color using same-parity bands near 0.77, 2.25 and 3.66 micrometres. Regional Asgard/Lindr coverage takes priority in overlap. USGS 2013 registered grids control geometry; missing cells remain missing. The view is neither natural color nor mineral abundance.

entries.subject: IAU/USGS Gazetteer centre-point export
entries.finding: Selected export supplies nomenclature labels, not terrain boundaries.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: USGS describes lunar-Lambert normalization of the mosaic without printing its values. Squyres and Veverka (1981) could not be opened, and the Callisto photometry of Belgacem and colleagues covers regions only. Callisto keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: A global disc-resolved Callisto law with its fitted emission range is read in the paper, or USGS publishes its lunar-Lambert values.

entries.subject: Protopapa et al. 2024 JWST carbon dioxide and hydrogen peroxide detections
entries.finding: Inspected the published study as a possible composition-map source. Its detections characterize disk-integrated spectra of the observed northern hemisphere; they do not supply resolved regional abundance maps. Painting regional deposits from these detections would invent spatial information.
entries.revisitWhen: A release provides spatially resolved measurements with body-coordinate registration, or a separately authorized non-spatial spectroscopy view makes the existing disk-integrated measurements useful.

entries.subject: USGS New Horizons 300 m monochrome mosaic
entries.finding: The selected 2017 LORRI/MVIC GeoTIFF supplies Monochrome. Its 300 m grid has variable observational resolution and existing Lunar-Lambert normalization to 15-degree phase; values are relative brightness, with original gaps and cast shadows retained.

entries.subject: USGS 300 m stereo and shape-from-shading terrain model
entries.finding: The signed terrain model supplies Elevation in metres above the 606 km sphere. The 300 m post spacing is not a terrain-accuracy claim; missing heights and mapping artifacts remain explicit.

entries.subject: PDS nh_charon_color_mosaic version 1.0
entries.finding: The original four-band floating array supplies enhanced false color using NIR/red/blue, not natural color. Its own metric coordinates, finite missing-data sentinel and common channel range are retained; the source mixes panchromatic detail and coarser color.

entries.subject: PDS nh_charon_bond version 1.0
entries.finding: The mapped product supplies modeled Bond albedo under the source scattering assumptions, with missing regions preserved. Its label summary incorrectly says Pluto; target, title, LIDVID and data identify Charon.

entries.subject: C_LEISA_HIRES and C_LEISA_LORRI_1 ice absorption views
entries.finding: The two closest scans supply Water ice and Ammonia from spectra, per-pixel wavelengths and geometry. Native sampling is about 5.0 and 8.6 km; spatial pooling further limits detail. Band strength is not abundance, and the weak ammonia signal is not a new mineral detection. Native FITS endian, unit and missing-value discrepancies remain documented.

entries.subject: Six earlier Charon LEISA scans
entries.finding: The retained source review surveyed metadata for six earlier scans with approximately 30–132 km native sampling. Their spectra were not processed or qualified; they cannot supply crater-scale detail.
entries.revisitWhen: A coarse-scale coverage question warrants processing their spectra and qualifying their geometry and calibration.

entries.subject: LEISA channels 199–207 and high-resolution segment
entries.finding: The ice recipes use channels 0–196. The archive warns that scattered-light calibration in the high-resolution segment, especially channels 199–207, is uncertain.
entries.revisitWhen: A calibration and applicable uncertainty assessment support the omitted segment for these scans.

entries.subject: Neighboring ready-made Pluto absorption maps
entries.finding: The neighboring ready-made absorption products inspected in the New Horizons archive target Pluto, not Charon. Charon composition views instead derive from its own LEISA scans.
entries.revisitWhen: A Charon-specific mapped absorption product with documented coordinates and processing is available.

entries.subject: Less-averaged LEISA display trial
entries.finding: The recorded visual trial showed stronger scan-pattern variation without establishing finer surface features. The selected spatial pooling and existing broad-signal texture dimensions were retained.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent spectral and spatial evidence shows that less pooling resolves real Charon structure above instrument and scan noise.

entries.subject: IAU Gazetteer and informal Organa mission landmark
entries.finding: The selected Gazetteer export supplies IAU places. Grundy et al. supplies the informal Organa centre at 310.9 degrees east, 54.3 degrees north, without an invented rim. Current features and minimaps share the photographic 0-degree east map edge.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Lunar-Lambert law of Buratti et al. (2017), A = 0.70 for LORRI (weight 0.5385 in the library's form), fitted at 15.08 to 16.85 degrees phase, relative to the flood-lit disc centre. The paper states no emission range; the limit 86.5 degrees is derived here from the outermost pixel of the finest Charon image in its Table 1 (LOR_0299147641) and is second class.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the published lunar-Lambert law of Buratti et al. (2017); Charon now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Hapke model of Buratti et al. (2019) as the limb law
entries.finding: w 0.72, g -0.09, roughness 23 degrees, fitted to disc-integrated phase curves from 15 to 169.5 degrees (ApJL 874, L3, Table 3). A disc-integrated fit states no emission range and was not tested on disc-resolved brightness; the disc-resolved lunar-Lambert fit of Buratti et al. (2017) is used instead.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved test of this Hapke model against LORRI images, with its emission range.

entries.subject: Published global infrared display mosaic
entries.finding: NASA PIA24027 is an 8192 by 4096 RGB equirectangular map centered at zero longitude. It combines Robidel 2020 VIMS infrared maps and Bland 2018 controlled ISS detail, with seams and artifacts removed by the producer. Used as a false-color photographic composite, not as a numeric spectral measurement.

entries.subject: Published photometrically corrected numeric spectral maps
entries.finding: Read the full author manuscript, sections 3 to 5, Table 3 and Figure 11; checked the publisher landing page and INAF repository. The paper describes median 0.5-degree footprint bins and wavelength-dependent photometric correction and says maps are online, but the inspected releases exposed the paper and raw PDS archive, not a retrievable numeric map product. The figure retains polar gaps and residual seams. No numeric map was extracted from its color legend.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numeric map with coordinates and missing-data definitions is located, or a separately validated reproduction of the published method is undertaken.

entries.subject: Enceladus super-resolution infrared mapping
entries.finding: The 2025 EPSC-DPS abstract describes revised navigation, global photometric correction and overlap-based super-resolution. The inspected conference and institutional records did not expose a downloadable map or reproducible processing release.
entries.revisitWhen: The numeric maps, navigation and method release become retrievable.

entries.subject: King, Fletcher and Ligier 2022 mapped VLT/SPHERE reflectance and composition fits
entries.finding: The 2026-09-13 intake established available numerical grids and deferred preparation. The 2026-09-14 implementation below is ready for local review; public inclusion remains deferred for explicit reuse terms. Implemented Ice signature as the measured reflectance ratio at the exact released wavelengths 1.30000/1.50263 micrometres (19,644 valid native nodes). Fine ice (0.1-0.3 mm) and Coarse ice (0.3-1 mm) are separate v1.0.2 posterior-median model components (19,616 valid nodes each), with their own 16th/84th-percentile bounds. The source uses east-positive 0-359 degree longitude and latitude -90 through 89 degrees; the paper's west-positive presentation is converted explicitly. One-degree resampling preserves cells and no-data but does not add detail beyond the approximately 150 km effective SPHERE resolution (about 25 km/px sampling). The release has no aggregate total-ice posterior: do not sum component medians or percentile bounds. Zenodo is other-open/Open Access, but no explicit numerical-data reuse licence was located. Use remains local scientific preview and private draft PR only; do not publish the assets.
entries.revisitWhen: Reopen if the authors or archive publish explicit numerical-data reuse terms or a replacement release. Preserve the exact ratio wavelengths, component-specific uncertainty and no-data; do not manufacture an aggregate ice posterior.

entries.subject: JWST carbon dioxide band depth
entries.finding: The current cube reducer maps eight public NIRSpec visits from November 2022 to February 2025, preserving finite coverage. This satisfies the former numerical-map acquisition condition; the continuum-relative depth is not an abundance retrieval.

entries.subject: USGS Voyager/Galileo 500 m global mosaic
entries.finding: Selected global GeoTIFF supplies Monochrome with published control, variable resolution, seams and gaps.

entries.finding: G1ESGLOBAL01, 12ESGLOCOL01 and 14ESGLOCOL01 supply False color only where registered three-band support is present.

entries.subject: USGS controlled Agenor DTM

entries.subject: USGS SIM 3513 Europa geologic units

entries.subject: Registered Galileo NIMS 17ENGLOBAL01A and 17ENGLOBAL02A CIOF observations
entries.finding: Two Minnaert-corrected registered observations supply Infrared within their documented coverage and registration limits.

entries.subject: Controlled Galileo CLEAR inserts in the existing Monochrome mosaic
entries.finding: 332 calibrated controlled products are acquired and decoded: 301 equirectangular and 31 whose inspected STAC records list only polar GeoTIFFs, on 6–629 m native grids. The original Monochrome view receives regional inserts; its existing global mosaic fills the remaining surface. At the unchanged detailed 8192×4096 geographic grid, 330 photographs supply 15.2238% of the sphere. Each contributor uses a bounded display gain fitted from co-located valid global-mosaic boundary pixels. Original illumination and registration uncertainties remain; no global photometric model is used. The separate Galileo dataset is removed. Geometry, renderer, eight dataset controls and existing texture dimensions stay unchanged. All 332 products were retrieved, byte-verified and decoded; two projection examples were freshly restored.

entries.subject: Replacing the global mosaic with controlled Galileo and Voyager images
entries.finding: Retrieved and decoded 379 selected CLEAR Galileo/Voyager maps. A trial 8K global mosaic reached 99.44% area coverage, but its brightness joins were worse than the retained Monochrome surface. A common display stretch did not solve different observed illumination. The final route retains the global mosaic and inserts controlled regional photographs within Monochrome. Voyager CLEAR and Galileo CLEAR have different spectral responses; their measured I/F is not assumed interchangeable. The global prototype is not delivered.
entries.revisitWhen: A released photometrically harmonized global product or a qualified cross-observation model resolves joins, spectral differences and terrain-dependent scattering while preserving source detail. Compare in the running app against the retained global mosaic before replacing it.

entries.subject: Lambert and terrain-specific Minnaert correction for a global Europa mosaic
entries.finding: The Lambert global trial produced unacceptable bright-edge clipping (roughly 19–25% in the tested variants). A Minnaert trial using ridged-plains parameters from Dhingra et al. (2021), followed by overlap gains, reduced some joins but did not qualify applying terrain-specific scattering parameters globally. Neither trial supplies production pixels. The regional inserts preserve original illumination and use bounded overlap-based display gains; no rejected physical correction supplies their pixels.
entries.revisitWhen: A model is supported for the selected filter, terrains and observation geometry, with source-backed applicability limits and improved matched browser evidence; do not retry globally extrapolated terrain parameters as a default.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Belgacem et al. (2020) give Hapke fits for 20 regions only (incidence and emission below 70 degrees), not a global law. Buratti and Veverka (1983) fitted a lunar-Lambert law to 90 Voyager images at 3 to 143 degrees phase, but only the abstract could be read, without the values or angle limits. Europa keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: The lunar-Lambert values and fitted angle ranges of Buratti and Veverka (1983), or another global disc-resolved Europa law, are read in the paper.

entries.subject: JWST 3.50 micrometre feature
entries.finding: The continuum-relative feature is displayed as Peroxide signature with the Yoffe and Shahaf 2026 instrumental-artifact dispute in the reader caption. Negative estimates are retained; this is not the published band-area method.

entries.subject: STIS 450 nm absorption
entries.finding: The current slit-scan reduction reproduces the 60-frame map, 82.3 percent coverage and the strongest feature beside Tara Regio. Irradiated sodium chloride is a spectral interpretation; an ocean origin is not established.

entries.subject: JunoCam 29 September 2022 flyby
entries.finding: Four released RGB-strip observations use the existing SPICE camera and limb refinement. Their observed illumination and missing footprint remain explicit.

entries.subject: Parked ALMA thermal map and additional sessions
entries.finding: The parked derived temperature grid was absent from the branch and public source cache. Two additional sessions were unfinished. An old colour image cannot substitute for its numeric product.
entries.revisitWhen: The numeric map is recovered with its reduction receipt, or the original calibrated data are reduced and independently checked.

entries.subject: Disputed Hubble plume-transit gallery
entries.finding: The parked gallery preparation was unfinished. Its disputed plume interpretation needs an explicit caption and completed source registration before inclusion.
entries.revisitWhen: The gallery is prepared and inspected with its dispute and registration evidence.

entries.subject: King and Fletcher 2022 mapped VLT/SPHERE reflectance and composition fits
entries.finding: The 2026-09-13 intake established available numerical grids and deferred preparation. The 2026-09-14 implementation below is ready for local review; public inclusion remains deferred for explicit reuse terms. Implemented Ice fraction (derived_total_ices) and Dark material (derived_total_synthetic) from the v1.0.1 posterior medians. Each native grid has 38,473 valid nodes, east-positive 0-359 degree longitude, latitude -90 through 89 degrees, -99 no-data and 16th/84th-percentile bounds. The converter retains no-data and uncertainty widths, reverses latitude and repeats only the seam; its one-degree resampling does not add detail beyond the paper's approximately 100-150 km effective resolution. The fit header names the 2015 observation, but the native fit mask is the four 2015/2021 0.95-1.65 micrometre reflectance masks' union minus five excluded 2015 nodes; the registration receipt records the pinned source hashes and coordinates. This establishes aggregate coverage correspondence, not a per-cell epoch contribution. These are model abundances, not uniquely detected species; individual salt fits remain degenerate. Zenodo is other-open/Open Access, but no explicit numerical-data reuse licence was located. Use remains local scientific preview and private draft PR only; do not publish the assets.
entries.revisitWhen: Reopen if the authors or archive publish explicit numerical-data reuse terms, corrected fit metadata, or a replacement release. Keep posterior bounds and no-data; do not present individual salts as identified deposits.

entries.subject: Bockelee-Morvan et al. 2024 JWST spectral mapping

This pass established a relevant paper, not a downloaded numerical surface-map release; coordinates, processing, masks and reuse were not verified.
entries.revisitWhen: Inspect the paper's data-availability route and retrieve the numerical map or reproducible source closure before selecting a surface quantity.

entries.subject: Juno UVS oxygen-emission brightness maps associated with Duling et al. 2026

Its observed OI 1356-Angstrom and combined OI 1304/1356-Angstrom brightness maps describe atmospheric emissions; a separate field estimates reflected sunlight using CII 1335 Angstrom. A longitude/latitude display grid alone does not make atmospheric emission a surface-composition measurement. Numerical files and altitude/line-of-sight treatment were not qualified.
entries.revisitWhen: Reconsider only for a scientifically supported observation view that preserves the atmospheric and reflected-light distinction; this is not a candidate for literal surface chemistry under the current fixed-scene scope.

entries.subject: New Horizons small-moon MVIC/LEISA composition products

entries.subject: USGS Voyager control network map

entries.subject: NASA Hyperion 3D model

entries.subject: NASA press mosaics

entries.subject: USGS Iapetus Cassini–Voyager 783 m mosaic

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Squyres et al. (1984) found a lunar-like law (Lommel-Seeliger, which has no parameter) adequate for Voyager images at 8 to 90 degrees phase, with a phase function that varies with albedo. Only the abstract could be read, so the emission range and the phase function are unknown. Iapetus keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: The fitted emission range of Squyres et al. (1984), or a Cassini disc-resolved Iapetus law with its ranges, is read in the paper.

entries.subject: USGS Voyager/Galileo 1 km monochrome mosaic
entries.finding: The selected GeoTIFF supplies Monochrome; published controlled and Lunar-Lambert-corrected values retain variable detail, seams and shadows.

entries.subject: USGS Voyager/Galileo 1 km false-color mosaic
entries.finding: The selected false-color GeoTIFF supplies False color; it combines Galileo ratios and Voyager/Galileo detail and is not a single-date natural-color observation.

entries.subject: Interpolated polar color in the USGS false-color mosaic

entries.revisitWhen: A product provides source-resolved polar color and a coverage mask.

entries.subject: USGS SIM 3168 Io geologic polygons
entries.finding: The selected polygon members supply the categorical Geology lens; no-data, unmapped poles and category conflicts remain missing, and colors are interpretive.

entries.subject: King et al. July 2019 VLT/MUSE 485 nm spectral-slope maps
entries.finding: Pinned native maps supply Spectral slope under the package interpretation record; first-valid-night coverage and residual night differences remain explicit.

entries.subject: King et al. July 2019 VLT/MUSE 560 nm absorption maps
entries.finding: Pinned native maps supply Visible absorption; the display does not turn the measured signal into composition abundance.

entries.subject: Juno JIRAM M-band (4.8 µm) night-side hot-spot map, orbits 41, 43, 47 and 49
entries.finding: Our reduction of 59 JIRAM frames, following Mura et al. (2024), supplies the Volcanic heat lens. 34 frames register to the sunlit limb; integrated hot-spot output matches the paper's Table 3 (median ratio 1.06 per orbit, 0.83 in the merged map) and 22 of 24 bright peaks lie within 3 degrees of a Davies et al. (2024) source. Coverage is 22% of Io, north and night side only. Revisit when: orbits 51 to 60 are reduced, or Mura et al. or the JIRAM team publish radiance maps as data.

entries.subject: Early JIRAM Io frames through the original sunlit-disc-fit route
entries.finding: Mura et al. (2024), Section 2.2: most images before orbit 37 are heavily saturated and fit only for locating hot spots, so their radiances are not mapped. A trial with them raised coverage to 49% but carried saturation streaks. That direct-RDR trial remains excluded. The separately qualified Perry registered-product route now retains unsaturated portions of early frames using published geometry, explicit detector masks and cold-column subtraction; it does not recover saturated values.
entries.revisitWhen: A saturation correction for early JIRAM Io frames is published, or the lens shows hot-spot locations rather than radiance.

entries.subject: Remaining JIRAM Io close-pass coverage in orbits 51 to 60
entries.finding: The existing mosaic tool already intersects the triaxial ellipsoid. Orbits 51 and 53 now contribute 31 registered frames. Trials of all 17 orbit-57 and 22 orbit-58 images produced no cells with three qualified night-side observations; partial-disc fits were too sparse. Volumes 59 and 60 were absent from the examined archive. Perry registered products now qualify PJ55 (42 accepted frames, 74,649 winning cells). Orbits 52 and 54 were indexed but not reduced; orbit 56 listed auxiliary products only. The current registered mosaic reaches 50.125S; remaining southern gaps are unqualified.
entries.revisitWhen: Additional sequences pass the existing registration and three-frame overlap checks, or a supported partial-disc registration method qualifies the 57/58 trials; revisit 59/60 when archive products are available.

entries.subject: Davies et al. (2024) Table A1 hot spots
entries.finding: No longer drawn: the symbol lens was replaced by measured JIRAM radiance. The table is kept byte for byte as an independent check of the map's hot-spot positions.
entries.revisitWhen: A lens shows catalogued hot-spot power as symbols again.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: The USGS false-colour mosaic page says a lunar-Lambert coefficient of 0.7 was adequate for all three colours, but gives no angle range and no fit. The disc-resolved studies (Simonelli and Veverka 1986 from Voyager; Simonelli, Dodd and Veverka 2001, Hapke fits to Galileo SSI) could not be opened, and Io's photometry varies strongly between regions. Io keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved Io law with its filter and fitted incidence, emission and phase ranges is read in the paper.

entries.subject: JIRAM May and July 2023 close-pass night-side volcanic radiance
entries.finding: 18 orbit-51 and 13 orbit-53 frames add roughly 7.6–15.5 km near-nadir sampling. A 0.25-degree map combines six visits, masks new detector samples at or above 10000 DN, and subtracts each qualified detector column's cold-night median before projection. Coverage is 24.12% of spherical surface area, reaching 11.125S. Of 41 peaks above 0.03 W/(m2 sr), 35 are within 3 degrees of catalogue hot spots; absolute radiometry, individual peak identities and resolved lava boundaries remain unqualified.

entries.subject: Perry et al. (2025) registered M-band FITS release through PJ55
entries.finding: All 2374 published M-band FITS frames in 27 orbit directories were screened. Published planetographic geometry and detector masks support 378 accepted frames on 17 contributing visits, covering 58.42% of spherical area on a 0.25-degree grid. Three native PDS comparisons match all radiance samples exactly after horizontal flipping. Cold-column medians and three-frame per-visit medians preserve the existing display scale; 60 of 72 bright local maxima match independent catalogue positions within 3 degrees. Mixed dates, smear, residual tracks, withheld saturation and southern gaps remain; absolute radiometry and total heat flow are not qualified.

entries.subject: Additional registered JIRAM coverage from daylight and distant images
entries.finding: The Perry release reports full M-band observational coverage, but the current night-side radiance mosaic admits 58.42% under its terminator, saturation, cold-column and overlap cuts. Distant images often lack 32 qualified cold samples in a detector column. Daylight subtraction and an alternative background method have not been qualified for this map; reducing those limits alone would admit unsupported radiance.
entries.revisitWhen: An independently checked reflected-sunlight removal or background estimator qualifies the excluded observations without saturation or reflection artifacts.

entries.subject: NASA/ESA Hubble WFC3 global map of 27 June 2019
entries.finding: The visible body uses the 3,600 by 1,800 map combining the 395, 502 and 631 nm filters; its published page excludes latitudes beyond 80 degrees, so preparation verifies measured rows 101 through 1,698 and carries the retained body to 80 degrees south and north, with four prepared high-latitude rings a side and eight-degree interior bands.

entries.subject: Hubble OPAL Cycle 32 F275W and FQ889N maps
entries.finding: The ultraviolet and methane-band lenses use the single-band FITS products observed 11 December 2025, preserving measured values including dark and finite negative samples, with a measured-pixel percentile stretch and false-colour palette for relative display contrast.

entries.subject: Validity of the OPAL exterior fill
entries.finding: The pinned maps contain exact-zero exterior fill but no separate validity extension, so only exact-zero regions connected to a polar source edge and non-finite samples are marked unavailable while isolated interior zeros remain observations; the README calls this a conservative, explicitly qualified interpretation of the source fill and an edge-fill heuristic without an independent validity mask.
entries.revisitWhen: A validity extension or mask accompanies the OPAL single-band maps.

entries.subject: JunoCam and JIRAM polar structure products
entries.finding: North-pole cyclone structure comes from PIA23808 and south-pole structure from PIA23556: both publications' false-colour or infrared palettes are discarded and only bounded luminance structure is transported, with chroma from the visible-light PIA24239 and PIA21382 products, credited to Emma Walimaki and John Landino under CC BY, and from the measured Hubble 64-degree edge.

entries.subject: Registration of the polar structure to the Hubble longitudes
entries.finding: The cyclone arrangements are source-backed but the Juno sources are not registered to the Hubble map's longitudes, so the polar views are structural illustrations rather than a new geodetic map; no absent Hubble pixel is presented as an observation.
entries.revisitWhen: A polar product registered to the Hubble longitude system is released.

entries.subject: IAU radii and the JUP365 ephemeris closure
entries.finding: The prepared scene binds the IAU equatorial and polar radii of 71,492 and 66,854 km and the JUP365 ephemeris closure, with 3.13 degrees of axial tilt and NASA's 9.9-hour rotation; the 36-second CSS rotation is an explicitly accelerated presentation timescale.

entries.subject: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Jupiter ring table
entries.finding: The checked table fixes ring boundaries, normal optical depths, vertical thicknesses and associated source moons, from the 100,000-122,400 km halo through the 270,000 km Thebe extension, and the prepared model preserves the physical optical-depth ordering.

entries.subject: Galileo PIA00701 and PIA01623 ring observations
entries.finding: PIA00701 establishes the three-part halo, main and gossamer structure, the halo's vertical extent and the truncation in Jupiter's shadow, and PIA01623 establishes the Amalthea and Thebe gossamer components and their approximately two-to-one edge-to-centre brightness; the prepared model composites those measured components once and retains their source thicknesses as metadata.

entries.subject: Contrast emphasis for the faint rings
entries.finding: Because the measured optical depths are orders of magnitude below an opaque surface, the presentation declares a log-optical-depth contrast emphasis capped at 0.4 alpha with a 0.65 exponent and a three-unit minimum width for the narrow main ring; the README states this is a visibility presentation, not a claim about how the rings would look to a nearby unaided observer, and every measured radial boundary and ordering is preserved.

entries.subject: OPAL Minnaert limb-darkening coefficients
entries.finding: The OPAL paper by Simon, Wong and Orton publishes the visible-map channel construction and empirical Minnaert coefficients, F631N k=0.999, F502N k=0.950 and F395N k=0.850, transcribed into a checked record while the copyrighted paper is linked rather than redistributed; preparation reapplies the channel-specific law for the current observer, preserving Jupiter's measured wavelength-dependent centre-to-limb behaviour.

entries.subject: PSG observation light direction as the presentation light
entries.finding: The pinned PSG configuration keeps its exact 4.360399-degree observation phase and light direction as source metadata, but that near-opposition geometry is not used as the free-orbit presentation light because it collapses the visible terminator into an unreadable limb; the presentation instead copies the accepted Saturn Sun direction as an authored choice.
entries.revisitWhen: A light direction derived from the observation geometry becomes usable for the free-orbit presentation.

entries.subject: Source-over photometric overlay
entries.finding: The prepared overlay keeps a 0.05 neutral-light ambient floor and a smoothstep terminator computed in linear light and re-encoded through sRGB as one source-over colour plus alpha; it is exact for the declared neutral reference channel value of 160 and otherwise a bounded photometric overlay, not per-texel spectral radiative transfer, which avoids inventing an unvalidated volumetric haze model.

entries.subject: Gaseous halo around the disc
entries.finding: The Hubble global map is already a visible-light map of the cloud atmosphere rather than a solid surface needing an Earth-like halo, and the checked 5 January 2024 full-disc Hubble view is the silhouette authority: 44,312 pixels in the normalized 1.005-to-1.03 exterior annulus are zero in every sampled channel, so the exterior halo is explicitly absent rather than artistically coloured.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured exterior halo is published for Jupiter at this geometry.

entries.subject: NASA GSFC Planetary Spectrum Generator configuration and I/F response
entries.finding: The checked configuration expands a pinned 2026/08/30 12:00 ephemeris seed and contains the 50-layer Moses et al. 2005 atmosphere from 10 bar to 10 nanobar; the R=240 I/F response has 253 samples from 0.35 to 0.998 micrometres, and the reflectance, temperature-pressure and phase charts are generated as static SVG before runtime.

entries.subject: JPL satellite catalogue and the Galileo PIA01299 montage
entries.finding: The checked JPL discovery and mean-elements snapshot retains its 115-satellite catalogue and the PIA01299 montage stays pinned source material, but because the shared runtime mounts exactly one detailed object scene, the dormant Jupiter-owned billboard and orbit-guide derivations are excluded from the active asset inventory; Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto have their own packages.
entries.revisitWhen: The shared runtime gains a contract for rendering a moon system inside a planet scene.

entries.subject: NASA/ESA/STScI/Amy Simon Hubble view of 5 January 2024
entries.finding: The navigation marker is the credited full-disc Hubble view, with its preparation recipe adapter-owned.

entries.subject: Dated test or browser run for this record
entries.finding: The evidence section states that the record describes image-background and source-value checks but cites no dated test or browser run; source byte pins are in the input manifest.
entries.revisitWhen: A dated test or browser run for this Jupiter version is recorded in the package.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hubble OPAL Minnaert coefficients of the visible map per channel (Simon et al. 2015, Table 1: F631N 0.999, F502N 0.95, F395N 0.85), relative to the flood-lit disc centre, without the former 0.05 ambient floor, smoothstep terminator or cap at the centre's brightness.

entries.subject: OPAL dated visible maps
entries.finding: Eleven released RGB maps from 2015 through 2025 use the shared date stepper and intersection of their three component footprints. The release sequence has no 2023 and two 2024 dates; no quantitative storm-size or colour trend is claimed.

entries.subject: JRM33 internal magnetic field
entries.finding: The PSH community degree-13 evaluator samples radial field at the 1-bar ellipsoid in System III east longitude. Zero is valid, the palette is linear, and the inferred internal field excludes external currents.

entries.subject: Militzer 2022 dilute-core interior
entries.finding: The gravity-inferred interior is not a surface map. A numerical radial profile and its model alternatives have not been qualified for the existing cross-section route in this change.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical profile and its assumptions are selected and checked.

entries.subject: Juno UVS or Hubble auroral grids
entries.finding: No new registered numeric auroral product was selected in this release.
entries.revisitWhen: A dated polar grid with units, geometry and an appropriate rendering interpretation is qualified.

entries.subject: Porter 2025 single-triaxial Kerberos interpretation
entries.finding: Presentation slide 7 refines the rounded abstract to full axes 14.5 × 8.2 × 7.2 km. The package retains this approximate ellipsoid without inferred local terrain; the source does not converge on a unique pole.

entries.subject: Porter 2025 contact-binary alternative and numerical mesh

entries.revisitWhen: A numerical Kerberos solution and its uncertainty, pole and coordinate conventions are released.

entries.subject: LORRI lor_0299153805 and lor_0299136735
entries.finding: The 2026-09-08 survey decoded and inspected both original calibrated FITS frames at native pixels: approximately 1.964 and 3.127 km/pixel, only a handful of independent samples across Kerberos. They constrain shape and integrated brightness but do not provide a registered surface albedo map.
entries.revisitWhen: Resolved surface information and a controlled pose permit a meaningful cartographic footprint for Kerberos.

entries.subject: NASA PIA20034 deconvolved portrait
entries.finding: The source account identifies interlacing, deconvolution and cosmetic enlargement described by the Science supplement. This portrait is observational context, not added independent surface samples or a camera solution.

entries.subject: MVIC, LEISA, HST and mapping-product source review
entries.finding: The retained flyby-literature and PDS survey qualified no registered color, spectral, topographic or geological Kerberos map. Disk-integrated measurements are not spatial textures, and this review does not establish that other observations do not exist.

entries.subject: C1138148 surface registration

entries.revisitWhen: A Larissa camera or surface-control release supports independent interior holdouts from a different viewing geometry.

entries.subject: Voyager ISS archive, C1138148

Limb-pointed registration is not independent surface-feature control; photographic terrain qualification remains deferred in the separate registration entry.

entries.subject: C1138142 and C1138153
entries.finding: Inspected archive frames. Excluded: repeated similar coverage or much coarser wide-angle sampling; no distinct dataset or useful added detail.
entries.revisitWhen: A Larissa observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Stooke n7larissa.tab radius grid
entries.finding: The PDS 5-degree west-positive radius grid supplies shape and radius-relative Elevation above 96 km. It preserves the published origin and modeled unseen shape; broad figure, exaggerated facets and depressions are not local altimetry or a high-resolution terrain survey.

entries.subject: NASA 2017 Cassini ISS monochrome map
entries.finding: Selected 5,760 by 2,880 map supplies Monochrome; black shadows remain observed because the published rectangular map has no validity mask.

entries.subject: NASA/JPL PIA18437 infrared-green-ultraviolet map
entries.finding: Selected 6,356 by 3,178 map supplies Enhanced color, with producer calibration and registration retained and no claim of natural color.

entries.subject: Mimas 2025 SPC Q128 OBJ
entries.finding: Selected complete Q128 OBJ supplies geometry and Shape; the 720-face simplification is a display approximation, not source uncertainty.

entries.subject: Mimas 2025 SPC radius GeoTIFF
