entries.subject: Schenk 2020 Voyager corrected mosaic
entries.finding: The losslessly retained mumap-cyl-180180.cub supplies Monochrome on its 240 m simple-cylindrical grid. It retains source photomet normalization, seams, camera marks, cast shadows and missing coverage; the 0–2400 DN stretch is display-only.

entries.subject: Schenk 2020 merged Miranda DEM
entries.finding: The losslessly retained mudem-ZT-cyl.cub supplies Elevation: merged stereogrammetry and photoclinometry in kilometres above the published ellipsoid. Its 240 m grid, source errors, smooth patches and missing samples do not establish uniform terrain accuracy.

entries.subject: Thomson and Baynham 2026 digitized historical map
entries.finding: The CC BY 4.0 GIS release supplies the historical Geology lens after its incompatible page CRS was reconstructed with six Miranda graticule fit intersections, six withheld intersections and three crater checks. It represents Voyager-era unit interpretation, not composition or terrain; coverage is about 44.2% and degree-scale registration limits remain.

entries.subject: JPL ura5vuu2.tif simulator map
entries.finding: The 1440 × 720 simulator display map is superseded by the denser Schenk mosaic and is not retained as a duplicate Monochrome lens.
entries.revisitWhen: A JPL release supplies a higher-detail, source-controlled Miranda map with documented projection and processing that improves on the selected Schenk mosaic.

entries.subject: PIA01490 south-polar and color press images
entries.finding: The press mosaics were examined as rendered-disc or press imagery; they do not establish a reusable registered surface map or global color coverage.
entries.revisitWhen: A primary release provides the underlying Miranda observations with reusable terms, body-fixed geometry and coverage adequate for independent registration.

entries.subject: USGS Miranda Voyager control network
entries.finding: The USGS control network is retained as registration support for the selected sources, not as a separate image or measured-scalar lens.

entries.subject: Historical geology registration limit
entries.finding: The retained 1.3–3.3 degree landmark differences are independent checks, not uncertainty bounds for every geological boundary; ambiguous source layer combinations remain missing.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-controlled Miranda geological release or additional independently identified controls can improve the page-to-body registration without converting source annotations or Z values into terrain.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet colour frames
entries.finding: 3 GEOMED frames in 1 complete sets (1.1 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color lens. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (1.03, 1.06); the archive calibration gives 0.927 and 1.056. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Helfenstein, Veverka and Thomas (1988) fitted Hapke models to Voyager whole-disc photometry of the five large Uranian moons. Only the abstract could be read (single-scattering albedo from 0.3 for Umbriel to 0.7 for Ariel, g near -0.3), and a whole-disc fit states no emission range. Schenk's 2020 mosaic history names ISIS photomet without its parameter file. Miranda keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved law for Miranda with its fitted emission range is read in the paper, or the photometric parameter file of Schenk's mosaic is released.

entries.subject: Hubble OPAL Cycle 32 2025 colour global map
entries.finding: The visible-detail globe uses the OPAL team's WFC3/UVIS F467M, F547M and F657N global map; the OPAL readme declares the TIFF arbitrarily scaled and contrast enhanced, so the normal lens does not publish those display values as literal true colour.

entries.subject: Irwin et al. (2024) true-colour Neptune reconstruction
entries.finding: Preparation matches the mean and channel variation of a checked equatorial OPAL sample to the unobscured central region of this true-colour reconstruction distributed by the Royal Astronomical Society; the CC BY 4.0 reference is committed under source/color/.

entries.subject: OPAL FQ619N methane-band global map
entries.finding: The methane lens uses the matching FQ619N global map, converted during preparation to fixed runtime rasters; the browser parses no FITS or TIFF.

entries.subject: OPAL F845M near-infrared global map
entries.finding: The near-infrared lens uses the F845M global map from the same OPAL release, prepared to fixed runtime rasters.

entries.subject: OPAL coverage near Neptune's north pole
entries.finding: Measured on the pinned 2025 OPAL maps: coverage ends near 71 degrees north and thins toward it. At 619 and 845 nm the rows from 60 to 57 degrees north still hold dark swath seams (darkest pixel 0.37 to 0.77 of the row median, settling at about 0.80 from row 67), and the colour map keeps near-black swath edges down to 42 degrees north (ratio 0.87 from row 98), so preparation starts the fill at 57 degrees north for the two bands and 41 degrees north for colour and extends that row toward its longitudinal mean at the pole, which recovers no polar detail. An earlier recipe continued from 30 degrees north, overwriting observed cloud bands between 30 and 60 degrees north, and flipped the two narrow-band maps upside down; both are fixed.
entries.revisitWhen: An OPAL or other global release observes Neptune's high northern latitudes.

entries.subject: IAU 2015 report radii
entries.finding: The prepared scene uses the 24,764 km equatorial and 24,341 km polar radii from the IAU 2015 report values.

entries.subject: JPL Solar System Dynamics satellite tables
entries.finding: JPL discovery, mean-elements and physical-parameter tables supply the prepared 16-moon catalogue, which stays pinned source material even though the shared runtime mounts one detailed object scene and does not carry moon-dot or orbit-bank derivations in its active closure.

entries.subject: PDS Rings Node Neptune ring table
entries.finding: The PDS Rings Node table supplies the prepared ring radii and widths.

entries.subject: NASA GSFC Planetary Spectrum Generator configuration and I/F response
entries.finding: Two panel charts are prepared from the committed PSG configuration and raw I/F response, and the third uses the pinned photometric phase coefficients.

entries.subject: NASA Science Neptune facts snapshot
entries.finding: The panel prose and facts are prepared from the committed NASA Science Neptune facts snapshot.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hubble OPAL Minnaert coefficients of the colour map per channel (F657N 0.50, F547M 0.80, F467M 0.88), the correction OPAL removed before projection, put back relative to the flood-lit disc centre.

entries.subject: Authored limb lighting: a 0.35 flood-light limb floor, an ambient term and a terminator ramp
entries.finding: Replaced by the OPAL Minnaert law of the colour map.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Dated Hubble OPAL visible-colour sequence (9 rotations)
entries.finding: One publisher RGB composite per included cycle, component FITS coverage, source-backed map frame and observation dates. Gray grid preserves missing coverage. Current scene lighting and rings remain a presentation, not the historical observing geometry. See the Hubble dates section of the README.

entries.subject: OPAL Cycles 22–23 dated maps
entries.finding: The TIFF and component FITS maps were acquired and inspected. Their red-channel Minnaert coefficient is 0.55 rather than the existing visible bank's 0.50; the 2015 map also starts at 180 degrees west longitude.
entries.revisitWhen: A separately prepared lighting bank for the older red-channel coefficient is in scope.

entries.subject: Kiss et al. (2016) representative triaxial family
entries.finding: The selected X=0.133 light-curve/thermal model gives a=(1+X)b and c=(1−X)b. Equal-volume normalization to JPL’s nominal 170 km radius yields derived semiaxes 193.76 × 171.01 × 148.27 km; these are not measured limb dimensions. The representative Figure 8 pole is one feasible solution and the prime meridian is arbitrary. Thermal roughness does not locate craters.

entries.subject: Kiss Figure 8 caption parameter discrepancy
entries.finding: The caption’s X=0.0133 conflicts with equation 4 and the repeated X=0.133 selection in sections 2.3, 3.4 and 4. The preparation follows the selected model in the text and preserves the discrepancy.
entries.revisitWhen: An author correction or underlying model record establishes which Figure 8 parameter is intended.

entries.subject: Voyager clear frames C1137631 and C1129120
entries.finding: The historical OPUS survey found 325 matches and retained its first 12 records. Calibrated native images C1137631 (43.27 km/pixel, 96.12° phase) and C1129120 (62.09 km/pixel, 55.74° phase) were inspected; their discs span roughly eight and five pixels. Illumination and sampling dominate, and pole/landmark registration is unqualified. No photographic lens is selected.
entries.revisitWhen: A controlled reconstruction demonstrates independent body-fixed registration and useful surface information at the native sampling, or a finer observation becomes available.

entries.subject: JPL texture inventory and mapped-product search
entries.finding: The inspected JPL Neptune texture inventory supplied no Nereid map, and the examined mapping releases and cited work did not yield a qualified terrain product. This bounded search does not establish that no other observations exist.
entries.revisitWhen: A linked Nereid map or shape release provides downloadable data with coordinates, quantity and coverage for inspection.

entries.subject: NASA PIA00054 size caption
entries.finding: The caption calls 170 km the distance across, conflicting with JPL’s 170 ± 25 km radius and the paper’s 335–345 km thermal effective diameters. The caption size is not used for geometry; effective thermal diameter is also not silently treated as volume diameter.
entries.revisitWhen: A corrected primary size record resolves the radius-versus-diameter discrepancy.

entries.subject: LORRI photograph as a photographic lens
entries.finding: A draft fitted only two detector translations, [+16.875, +0.5] pixels, with the PDS camera, PCK pose and released mesh fixed. Reversing the transfer, its two held regions preferred shifts 1.414 and 5.099 pixels away, and the released mesh-to-kernel frame binding is unverified.
entries.revisitWhen: The mesh-to-kernel frame binding is verified and the registration passes interior holdouts in both transfer directions.

entries.subject: MVIC colour sequence as a colour lens
entries.finding: New Horizons' only MVIC colour scan of Nix, MC0_0299171078_0X536_SCI at 100,464 km, has 19.8 microradian pixels (Ralph instrument kernel) or 1.99 km each, so Nix's 48.4 x 33.8 x 31.5 km model spans 24 x 17 x 16 pixels; the red region is a few pixels. That is smaller than one band-alignment patch (13-pixel radius, 9-pixel search), so neither cross-band nor image-to-mesh registration can be measured, and a lens would carry colour 6.6 times coarser than the LORRI lens (0.30 km per pixel, 161 x 113 pixels). The closest MVIC scan, MP2_0299178462 at 0.45 km per pixel, is panchromatic.
entries.revisitWhen: A calibrated colour observation resolves Nix at least as finely as its LORRI lens.

entries.subject: Porter 2021 released shape model
entries.finding: The released 40,002-vertex STL supplies geometry. Its unitless extent agrees with the paired paper under an explicitly inferred 500 m per source unit. This scale agreement does not verify the STL-to-IAU frame binding.

entries.subject: New Horizons nh_pcnh_010.tpc active V008 orientation
entries.finding: The recovered PDS kernel supplies the active V008-derived orientation for the diagnostic image projection at target emission time. Commented V009 alternatives are explicitly unverified and are not selected; recovered inputs do not qualify photographic registration.

entries.subject: New Horizons small-moon MVIC/LEISA composition products
entries.finding: The retained source review treats these products as scientific context; it did not qualify a spatial composition map on the released 2021 mesh. This does not establish that observations are absent.
entries.revisitWhen: A target-specific composition product has interpretable calibration, coordinates and qualified transfer onto this source mesh.

entries.subject: Porter et al. 2025 updated model and albedo work
entries.finding: The retained review located the 2025 work but no downloadable updated mesh, albedo raster or matched camera solution usable for the 2021 STL. This is the recorded search outcome, not a renewed claim that no release exists.
entries.revisitWhen: The numerical model, albedo or camera release is located with its coordinate and version bindings.

entries.subject: Schenk/LPI 2020 oumap-cyl-180180.cub
entries.finding: Included as Monochrome. Updated control network and native numeric samples make it preferable to the older display-texture map. The release supplies photometrically corrected imagery; preserved shadows and seams are disclosed.

entries.subject: Schenk/LPI 2020 oumapZlimb.cub
entries.finding: Excluded as an Elevation lens. These are sparse digitized limb profiles, not extended surface elevation coverage. The author warns that their older control network may displace them by several degrees. They must not be expanded into neighboring terrain or treated as a registered full-surface DEM.
entries.revisitWhen: A released Oberon topographic reconstruction provides extended measured coverage registered to the selected mosaic; sparse limb values alone cannot fill that gap.

entries.subject: Schenk and Moore 2023 topography overview and 2020 source paper
entries.finding: Supporting scientific context. The authors explicitly describe the lack of extended topography on Oberon and Umbriel, confirming why this package has no Elevation lens. Paper figures are not substitutes for measured raster coverage.

entries.subject: JPL simulator Oberon texture, 1440 × 720, 4 pixels/degree
entries.finding: Superseded as a display source. It derives from USGS/Voyager grayscale imagery, but does not provide the selected release's revised control metadata and floating-point source values. Its nominal pixel count is not evidence of more native detail. No duplicate lens is added.
entries.revisitWhen: A better controlled JPL release provides observed detail or coverage beyond the selected Schenk mosaic.

entries.subject: PDS Voyager 2 Uranus ISS EDR archive
entries.finding: Underlying observation archive, excluded from this presentation in favor of the already corrected and controlled release. Raw frames would require a separate radiometric and pointing reconstruction; PDS warns about errors in original emission/incidence metadata.
entries.revisitWhen: A Oberon observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Voyager C2683625 / C2683627 / C2683629 color reconstruction
entries.finding: The 2026-09-07 trial used calibrated GEOMED CLEAR C2683625, VIOLET C2683627 and GREEN C2683629 (about 5 km/pixel, roughly 300-pixel disc), following the Helfenstein photometry route. Final image-space RMS was 0.55, 0.86 and 1.07 pixels respectively. Despite bounded Lunar-Lambert correction and missing unstable limb samples, mounted color views were softer than Monochrome, with chromatic fringes and a visible coverage transition. This trial did not qualify a second lens.
entries.revisitWhen: A sharper reconstruction with independently validated inter-band registration removes the chromatic fringes and visible coverage transition without borrowing monochrome detail.

entries.subject: JPL PIA00034 color disc
entries.finding: Excluded from mapped lenses. The published disc reconstructs color from violet, clear and green filters; the press image alone does not supply a calibrated, registered surface product or new coverage.
entries.revisitWhen: A Oberon observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Geologic map manuscript catalog
entries.finding: Unresolved interpretive candidate. The catalog records a manuscript color plate but supplies no downloadable qualified geospatial units or source projection/coverage metadata. It is not used as a scientific raster.
entries.revisitWhen: The catalog’s linked manuscript data become downloadable with geospatial units, projection, coverage and reuse terms.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet colour frames
entries.finding: 3 GEOMED frames in 1 complete sets (21.7 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color lens. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (0.935, 0.915); the archive calibration gives 0.870 and 0.921. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Helfenstein, Veverka and Thomas (1988) fitted Hapke models to Voyager whole-disc photometry of the five large Uranian moons. Only the abstract could be read (single-scattering albedo from 0.3 for Umbriel to 0.7 for Ariel, g near -0.3), and a whole-disc fit states no emission range. Schenk's 2020 mosaic history names ISIS photomet without its parameter file. Oberon keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved law for Oberon with its fitted emission range is read in the paper, or the photometric parameter file of Schenk's mosaic is released.

entries.subject: Cassini 2023 SPC shape and radius products
entries.finding: Selected paired products supply Shape and Radial height under their documented source frame and support masks.

entries.subject: Cassini 2023 SPC albedo and quality products
entries.finding: Selected relative albedo, maplet resolution and image-count products retain support limits and are not natural color or uncertainty.

entries.subject: Cassini VIMS IR 1465671822_1
entries.finding: Accepted cube supplies Infrared and Ice absorption from 41 supported native pixels with coarse registration limits.

entries.subject: Cassini VIMS IR 1465670650_1 fit
entries.finding: The recorded fit has systematic independent holdout bias and does not inherit the accepted correction.
entries.revisitWhen: A new fit passes independent holdouts under documented geometry.

entries.subject: SBIB regional RGB candidate
entries.finding: Different ellipsoid and shape convention lack qualified RGB-to-2023-shape registration.
entries.revisitWhen: Source-specific registration with independent controls qualifies the candidate.

entries.subject: Older DLR mosaic and Gaskell Q128 source
entries.finding: Earlier Monochrome is not draped onto the changed centre and shape because it would mix source frames.
entries.revisitWhen: A frame-qualified registration to the selected shape is released.

entries.subject: Cassini ISS narrow-angle photograph N1465662798_2 through SPICE kernel cameras
entries.finding: One CISSCAL-calibrated clear-filter frame from the June 2004 approach, 0.466 km per pixel from 77,935 km at 86 degrees phase, cast through a kernel camera refined to the lit limb by 0.0095 degrees. The relief sweep against the shape places it at -0.75 degrees with peak correlation 0.76 and is decisive; the registration verdict needs three decisive frames, so this single-frame lens has none. Coverage is 14.6 percent of the surface, the sunlit half of one side.

entries.subject: Eight Cassini ISS approach frames, one per 45 degrees of longitude, as one mosaic
entries.finding: All eight frames (0.47 to 1.53 km per pixel, 85 to 92 degrees phase) pass limb refinement with 24 controls against the 2.5 pixel holdout budget once three frames that failed it were replaced (N1465668427 runs off the detector, N1465641880 left 3.76 px RMS, N1465662846 matched 59.5 percent of holdout points). The mosaic fails level matching: after Lommel-Seeliger normalization, consecutive approach frames differ by log ratios of -0.31 and -0.36 in their overlaps, and the fitted gains span 0.51 to 1.32 against a 1.5 budget. A disk function that does not hold at about 90 degrees phase is the likely cause; not verified.
entries.revisitWhen: A published Phoebe photometric model valid near 90 degrees phase normalizes the overlaps within the level-matching budget.

entries.subject: NASA/JHUAPL/SwRI New Horizons Ralph/MVIC global colour mosaic
entries.finding: The Color lens uses the three-filter global mosaic published 20 January 2017, north up with Sputnik Planitia near the centre; it is the published colour product, not calibrated true-colour reflectance.

entries.subject: USGS LORRI/MVIC global mosaic, July 2017
entries.finding: Monochrome uses the 24,888 by 12,444 equirectangular mosaic with positive-east 0-360 degree longitude, which reserves zero for gaps.

entries.subject: USGS New Horizons stereo DEM at 300 m
entries.finding: Elevation uses signed 16-bit metres above a 1,188.3 km sphere with -32,768 as no data, read through a TIFF reader that checks signedness, compression, strip bounds and no-data metadata; the authored blue/tan/red palette is linear at -8/0/+8 km and clips outside, and shading comes from the same signed DEM with no vertical exaggeration and no invented slope where a neighbour is missing.

entries.subject: Drozdov and Emelyanov (2026) LEISA four-material Hapke fit, baseline least-squares solution
entries.finding: The three ice lenses use params_ls.fits and its matching error file from the CC BY 4.0 Zenodo release, modelled surface fractions from five calibrated New Horizons LEISA scans of 14 July 2015 on a common 0-100 percent scale; extensions 1-3 hold methane-rich, nitrogen-rich and water-ice area fractions and no Hapke inversion, sharpening, detail injection or smoothing runs here.

entries.subject: Chi-squared alternative fit in the same release
entries.finding: The authors prefer the least-squares solution over the chi-squared fit, which creates a strong polar discontinuity, and alternative fits are not extra dataset rows.
entries.revisitWhen: The authors publish a preferred alternative solution or a revised release.

entries.subject: Temperature, grain sizes and the tholin proxy
entries.finding: Temperature is excluded because the paper identifies unphysical upper-bound solutions, and grain sizes and the tholin proxy lie outside this three-ice view.
entries.revisitWhen: A release resolves the unphysical temperature solutions or the view is extended beyond three ices.

entries.subject: Coordinate registration of the LEISA maps
entries.finding: The FITS headers omit WCS, so the nearly 2:1 array is mapped over the full sphere from section 2.4's 7 km equirectangular description and Figure 6's east-increasing, north-up orientation; the Sputnik feature, blank footprint and northern averages agree in that orientation, but this is regional map registration and the release provides no subpixel coordinate metadata.
entries.revisitWhen: The release or a successor publishes coordinate metadata for the LEISA maps.

entries.subject: Uncomputed LEISA cells and the error cutoff
entries.finding: Uncomputed cells are finite rather than NaN and carry a complete initialization tuple, including an impossible negative solubility, repeated in the error file and matching Figure 6's blank footprint; the whole tuple is withheld in 335,273 cells, valid low fractions are kept, and a component error is required to be finite and between 0 and 100 percentage points as an explicit display choice rather than an author confidence threshold.

entries.subject: Independent Astropy and NumPy decoding check
entries.finding: The LEISA reader matches 192 independent Astropy 8.0.1 and NumPy 2.5.3 sample decisions and the accepted cell counts for all three maps, and the unchanged native maps give 69.31 percent methane-rich and 19.88 percent nitrogen-rich ice averaged over 60-90 degrees north against the paper's rounded 69 and 20 percent; these checks establish decoding, sampling and the declared mask, not the authors' spectral inversion.

entries.subject: Model and calibration uncertainty in the ice fractions
entries.finding: The fractions depend on assumed ice optical properties and the fitting method; the paper reports residual scan seams and sensitivity of Sputnik Planitia's nitrogen fraction to the assumed nitrogen absorption, formal errors do not include every model or calibration uncertainty, and the nominal 7 km cells with varying effective resolution cannot support close-up geological detail.
entries.revisitWhen: A revised fit or new observations reduce the model and calibration uncertainty.

entries.subject: Incomplete and uneven map coverage
entries.finding: Neither mosaic nor the DEM covers all of Pluto, so a neutral gray cartographic grid marks identified gaps, painted before packing and never interpolated; for the colour JPEG only exactly black pixels connected to the southern border are marked, so a dark boundary fringe can remain and nonzero dark pixels are preserved without inpainting.
entries.revisitWhen: A global product with complete Pluto coverage, or a validity mask for these maps, is released.

entries.subject: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature centre points
entries.finding: Named features use the Pluto centre-point export, snapshot 2026-09-11 and public domain per its FGDC metadata; preparation verifies the archive, reads the attribute table and datum, drops the albedo-feature type code and folds repeated rows, and labels depend on their size on screen.

entries.subject: English Wikipedia lead summaries as caption notes
entries.finding: 21 labelled names carry a caption note from the CC BY-SA 4.0 Wikipedia lead summary retrieved 2026-09-12, joined through Wikidata's Gazetteer id property and pinned with the article link and revision.

entries.subject: Pinned JPL physical parameters and NASA Pluto facts
entries.finding: Physical facts come from the selected JPL row values and NASA's facts record, checked during preparation: radius 1,188.3 km, density 1.853 g/cm3, sidereal rotation -6.3872 days and orbital period 247.92065 years, with the 39.482 AU solar semimajor axis from the Pluto row of JPL's approximate-positions Table 1 (since dropped from JPL's page; checked against the archived table); the body record carries the NSSDC obliquity of 119.51 degrees while pole, prime meridian and Sun direction come from the IAU/WGCCRE rotation model.

entries.subject: Atmospheric haze material
entries.finding: Lighting is the Mercury-style Lambert bank with a Shadows toggle and no atmosphere material, so Pluto's real haze layers are not modelled and the sky orientation is contextual rather than a New Horizons camera solution.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-backed haze model suitable for prepared material is adopted.

entries.subject: Charon and Pluto's other moons
entries.finding: Pluto is a standalone dwarf planet in the shared object shell and the other moons are not mounted; the package is a source-backed presentation, not an epoch-specific ephemeris or a pixel-identical recreation of another renderer.
entries.revisitWhen: The shared runtime gains a contract for mounting a moon system with a body.

entries.subject: Dated report for this version
entries.finding: The retained notes point to unit and browser checks and mention separate capture reports, but identify no dated report here, and test definitions are not passing-run evidence.
entries.revisitWhen: A dated run for this Pluto version is recorded in the package.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Lunar-Lambert law of Buratti et al. (2017), A = 0.70 for LORRI (weight 0.5385 in the library's form), fitted at 15.08 to 16.85 degrees phase, relative to the flood-lit disc centre. The paper states no emission range; the limit 86.8 degrees is derived here from the outermost pixel of the finest Pluto image in its Table 1 (LOR_0299124574) and is second class.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the published lunar-Lambert law of Buratti et al. (2017); Pluto now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Voyager clear GEOMED frames C1137317 and C1138920
entries.finding: The calibrated, geometrically corrected clear frames supply complementary coarse Monochrome coverage. Native detector scales are 1.35 and 8.03 km/pixel; the close frame has dark-current background and low signal, and neither frame establishes feature-controlled terrain.

entries.subject: Voyager violet C1137328, blue C1137339 and green C1137350
entries.finding: The three calibrated GEOMED frames supply a separate coarse filter-color lens after per-frame geometry, limb and held-out-sector checks. The roughly 60-pixel discs, long exposures and common-interior mask prohibit clear-frame detail transfer, white balance or pan-sharpening.

entries.subject: Stooke n8proteus.tab global radius grid
entries.finding: The PDS 5-degree west-positive radius grid supplies the shape and radius-relative Elevation lens above 208 km. It represents broad Voyager-derived shape; modeled unseen terrain, possible facet/depression exaggeration and lack of geoid or local altimetry remain explicit.

entries.subject: Ted Stryk Proteus color composite
entries.finding: The inspected composite is CC BY-NC-ND and supplies no permission to reproject or redistribute derivatives, so it is not used as a texture.
entries.revisitWhen: The author or a compatible primary release grants derivative reuse and provides source pixels plus body-fixed registration that improve on the retained Voyager frames.

entries.subject: Stooke shaded-relief drawings
entries.finding: The radius grid is used for shape/Elevation, but its interpretive shaded-relief drawings are not treated as photographic imagery.
entries.revisitWhen: A separately documented measured scalar product with its own grid, units and coverage supports a distinct Proteus lens.

entries.subject: Stooke 1994 links and USGS/PDS map candidates
entries.finding: The survey did not qualify a separately registered color, altimetric DEM or composition product; the linked 1994 paper download was unavailable and absent linked data are not claimed nonexistent.
entries.revisitWhen: The original paper or a linked Proteus dataset becomes accessible with documented provenance, coordinates, quantity and reuse terms for source inspection.

entries.subject: Clear and filter-color photographic registration
entries.finding: Limb, outline and inter-band checks support coarse observed brightness only. They do not provide independent cartographic feature control; retained frame-centre fits and held-out RMS are not a photographic terrain qualification.
entries.revisitWhen: A Proteus camera or surface-control release supports independent interior holdouts from a meaningfully different viewing geometry without weakening the registration criteria.

entries.subject: USGS Rhea Cassini–Voyager 417 m mosaic
entries.finding: Rhea_Cassini_Voyager_mosaic_global_417m.tif supplies Monochrome. Its actual 764.1 km projection sphere, 180 degrees east left edge, exact-zero gaps, source seams and shadows remain.

entries.subject: NASA/JPL PIA18438 2014 enhanced-color map
entries.finding: The 12,015 by 6,008 ultraviolet/infrared Cassini map supplies Enhanced color. Producer calibration, registration and photometric correction are retained; it is not natural color and has no separate mask.

entries.subject: Weirich et al. 2025 Rhea SPC Q128 OBJ
entries.finding: rhea_128_o.obj supplies Shape. The 2,000-face regularize:false presentation and 7,635 m limit are display approximation choices, not source uncertainty.

entries.subject: Weirich et al. 2025 Rhea SPC radius grid
entries.finding: rhea_radius_g.tif supplies Elevation as centre-relative radius minus the 763.5 km source sphere; its actual east/south edge strips remain unfilled.

entries.subject: Weirich et al. 2025 Rhea SPC relative-albedo grid
entries.finding: rhea_albedo_g.tif supplies dimensionless Relative albedo. It is normalized near one, affected by terrain and shadows, less validated than topography, and not calibrated reflectance.

entries.subject: Scipioni and Combe Rhea Cassini VIMS mosaic collection
entries.finding: rhea_notnorm_pc_modified_2 supplies false-color Infrared and continuum-relative Ice absorption with archived wavelengths and phase parameters; missing values remain missing.

entries.subject: Absolute Rhea VIMS registration
entries.finding: Fractions-of-a-source-pixel absolute registration remain unresolved; source reading checks do not qualify that alignment.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent controls establish the VIMS source frame against the selected body presentation.

entries.subject: Hubble OPAL Cycle 32 rotation-A global map of 2025-08-29
entries.finding: The body map is the archive's 1,800 by 900 F395N/F502N/F631N composite, resampled with a Lanczos-3 kernel to the 2,880 by 1,440 grid and retained byte-identical under the package's observations directory, with the declared solar colour applied in linear light.

entries.subject: Unobserved rows in the OPAL visible map
entries.finding: The map never observed rows 0-35 north of 82.8 degrees, rows 431-444 behind the rings and rows 887-899 south of 87.4 degrees; the geometry recipe names those rows and preparation fills them by linear interpolation in latitude between the nearest observed rows, detecting nothing from pixel values, and the rotation-B map of the same year has the same gaps so it cannot fill them.
entries.revisitWhen: An OPAL or other global release observes those latitude rows.

entries.subject: NASA Cassini PIA21611 north-polar projection
entries.finding: The 2017 Cassini north-polar map was removed from the default visible body because it produced a visibly separate, cross-mission cap over the 2025 Hubble OPAL map. Both prepared polar caps now project the same OPAL surface after its declared unobserved rows are filled.
entries.revisitWhen: A separate Cassini-era dataset view is requested with a coherent body map and presentation.

entries.subject: Cassini UVIS HSP alpha Virginis occultation, 2006 day 285
entries.finding: Ring opacity is the 1 km-bin normal optical depth profile: of 73,713 bins between 66,900 and 140,612 km, 60,886 carry a measured depth, 4,518 are clean bins below the detection floor and count as empty and 8,309 are flagged corrupted and interpolated from neighbours, each becoming a transmission byte of 255 times exp of minus the optical depth; the Encke and Keeler gaps, the Cassini division and the F ring now come from this occultation rather than the retired hand-authored clearings.

entries.subject: Radius-indexed ring colour dataset
entries.finding: No qualified radial colour dataset exists: the Cassini ISS natural-colour ring mosaics in the Photojournal are perspective views rather than radius-indexed strips, so the ring colour is uniform white under the declared solar tint.
entries.revisitWhen: A radius-indexed ring colour or reflectance profile is released.

entries.subject: Hubble OPAL F225W and FQ889N single-band maps
entries.finding: The ultraviolet and methane lenses use the pinned 1,800 by 900 single-band maps, keeping rotation A intact rather than averaging temporally separated cloud detail with rotation B, filling only unmeasured polar and ring-occluded rows in the same longitude, applying a declared false-colour palette and a pansharpening pass clamped to 0.88-1.12 so the Hubble maps keep authority over broad spectral luminance; they are source-backed spectral interpretations, not pure single-band products or natural colour.

entries.subject: Hubble WFC3 programme 17843 ring frames of 2025-08-29
entries.finding: The broad ring response is cross-checked against ifcu37ccq in F225W, ifcu37cdq in F631N and ifcu37ceq in FQ889N, and the prepared lens textures modify broad ring-band colour and luminance while retaining the UVIS alpha profile, narrow gaps, ringlets and readability floors.

entries.subject: Replacement profiles for the D, G and E rings
entries.finding: Hubble does not resolve a complete replacement profile for the D, G and E rings in these frames, so those details remain qualified visible-light morphology.
entries.revisitWhen: A dataset resolves complete D, G and E ring profiles.

entries.subject: Thermal view as an explicit illustration
entries.finding: The thermal view is schematic, prepared from visible luminance, cloud-window contrast and authored latitude and longitude patterns; no Cassini detector samples or measured global thermal raster enter it, its colour is illustrative intensity rather than infrared brightness or temperature, and the visible label and legend state that distinction.

entries.subject: Cassini VIMS high-contrast infrared scan PIA17468
entries.finding: The scan was considered as a physical reference but is a narrow observed swath in a particular viewing geometry, not a registered global thermal map suitable for this globe, so it remains a reference rather than a texture input.
entries.revisitWhen: A registered global infrared map suitable for this globe is released.

entries.subject: Global CIRS temperature map
entries.finding: The existing sources do not qualify a global CIRS temperature map; the README records it as unresolved rather than claiming such a dataset does not exist.
entries.revisitWhen: A qualified global CIRS temperature map is located or released.

entries.subject: Mankovich and Fuller (2021) diffuse-core result and Movshovitz density profiles
entries.finding: The interior radial presentation follows the 2021 ring-seismology diffuse-core interpretation, which places the stable core-envelope transition out to about 60 percent of Saturn's radius, cross-checked against the CC0 Movshovitz density profiles, with composition and terminology checked against the NASA/JPL-Caltech interior cutaway illustration and no pixels from it redistributed; the visible radii and colours are declared presentation choices, not hard boundaries or measured colours.

entries.subject: One schematic bank for the interior layers
entries.finding: The structural section, metallic-hydrogen and diffuse-core textures share one schematic bank because none of the observation lenses measures below Saturn's atmosphere, and the declared false-colour responses of the other lenses do not recolour the unobserved deep layers.

entries.subject: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Saturn ring statistics
entries.finding: The published PDS boundaries constrain the Cassini and Roche divisions, the Encke and Keeler gaps and the F ring, whose 140,224 km core uses the PDS optical-depth range rather than a painted line; the prepared image extends through the F ring's 140,612 km outer boundary and keeps the documented D-ring ringlets at 67,580 and 71,710 km with their existing 105 km footprint.

entries.subject: Prepared opacity and extrema emphasis in the rings
entries.finding: Across the C-ring interval from 74,500 to 91,975 km preparation remaps source alpha with 1-(1-alpha)^2.25 and a DPR-2 local-extrema pass gives salient one-pixel ringlets and gaps a two-CSS-pixel minimum footprint, applied to light and dark extrema alike; source radii, band widths, shadow sampling and ring-plane geometry are unchanged, and the README calls these prepared opacity emphases rather than physical optical-depth claims, with Keeler still source-limited.

entries.subject: IAU radii, SAT441 kernel and the prepared time scale

entries.subject: Colour tie of the OPAL visible map to Karkoschka's 1995 whole-disc spectrum
entries.finding: The OPAL colour TIF is arbitrarily scaled per channel and rendered 1.4 times too blue (map mean blue/red 0.65 in linear light). Karkoschka's full-disc albedo of Saturn (phase 5.7 degrees, rings edge-on, PDS 1995LOW.TAB) times a 5,772 K Planck spectrum through the CIE 1931 observer gives linear sRGB 0.6168, 0.4713, 0.2982 (#ceb794), green/red 0.7640 and blue/red 0.4834. Divided by the limb law's disc means (0.7694, 0.8698, 0.7354) the map targets are green/red 0.6759 and blue/red 0.5057; the solar-tinted map measured 0.9272 and 0.6953 (cosine-weighted, linear), so the gains are red 1, green 0.729, blue 0.7273. The swatch's independent Payne et al. (2026) spectrum agrees under a D65 white: green/red 0.863 and blue/red 0.589 against Karkoschka's 0.863 and 0.593.

entries.subject: Tying the map's own mean colour, rather than the lit disc, to Karkoschka's whole-disc colour
entries.finding: Karkoschka measured the disc with its limb darkening; OPAL divided each filter's darkening out and the overlay puts it back per channel, so a map mean tied straight to the whole-disc ratios (gains green 0.824, blue 0.6952) renders a disc of green/red 0.856 instead of 0.764 and an olive limb (a* -5 at 0.85-0.95 of the radius) in a preview built with the lane's own surface and limb code.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing while the lighting overlay puts back a per-channel limb law.

entries.subject: Minnaert coefficient for the visible map's blue channel
entries.finding: The blue channel uses F467M's k 0.86 from the OPAL Cycle 32 README table ("F467M 0.86 .00507"), the README filter closest to the sRGB blue primary. F395N's 0.40 is violet light that carries 13 % of the true-colour blue channel in Saturn's sunlit spectrum; with it the limb brightened in blue and turned grey-blue (b* -16 at the rim, 0.95-0.99 of the radius) in the app. The map's blue data are still F395N.

entries.subject: Brightness of the colour-tied visible map
entries.finding: The tie keeps red and lowers green and blue, so the map lost a fifth of its cosine-weighted luminance (0.426 to 0.337) and Saturn looked brown in the app (whole-disc Y 0.315 against 0.409 on main). The tied map now gets back its untied mean luminance with one factor on all three channels, 1.264, then a soft shoulder, 0.8 + 0.2 (1 - exp(-(m - 0.8) / 0.2)), on each texel's brightest channel, all channels by the same amount: 4.35 % of texels, none clipped, ratios kept. The factor alone clips red on 0.5 % of texels; the largest factor that clips nothing, 1.085, leaves the whole disc at Y 0.326. Chosen by the user on a preview built with the lane's own code, 2026-09-25.

entries.subject: Level reference for the Voyager color lens: Rings Node GEOMED I/F against Bland's voycal I/F

entries.subject: Akatsuki UVI 365 nm Level 3b exposure as the ultraviolet cloud lens

Brightness is the stated transform (radiance x 5e-9) ^ (1/2.2) with white at 2.0e8 W/m2/sr/m, above the exposure's measured maximum 1.8116e8, so nothing clips; there is no photometric normalisation, contrast enhancement or sharpening. entries.subject: Limb halo outside the cloud deck
entries.finding: The halo is a NASA PSG limb profile of PSG's Venus template (VIRA-45 with its sulfuric acid haze), computed on 2026-09-25 with a local nasapsg/psg container: single scattering (NMAX 0, LMAX 41) on 1 km beams at 8 tangent altitudes from the 75 km cloud top to 120 km, the Sun one degree above the tangent point horizon behind the observer, divided by PSG's multiple-scattering disc centre (NMAX 6, LMAX 41, what PSG asks for these aerosols) under an overhead Sun, each band the mean of 5 nm windows. Relative to the disc centre it is 0.039, 0.068 and 0.110 (red, green, blue) at 75 km, 0.016, 0.030 and 0.051 at 80 km and 0.0017, 0.0032 and 0.0057 at 90 km. The first local runs were flat because PUMAS fell back to a two-stream solver for memory and the Sun sat on the horizon; both are now refused by the tool.

entries.subject: A measured limb halo to replace the PSG model
entries.finding: No calibrated limb radiance profile of Venus near full phase in visible bands was found. Pioneer Venus OCPP limb scans at 365 and 690 nm (Lane and Opstbaum 1983) and Venus Express VMC limb images at 513 nm were taken at other phase angles and wavelengths, so they can check the haze height but cannot replace the model.
entries.revisitWhen: A calibrated Venus limb radiance profile in visible bands near full phase is published or archived.

entries.subject: Magellan global microwave emissivity
entries.finding: The USGS 4641 m signed GeoTIFF is decoded as (DN-1)/10000 with its declared nodata and projection. Antenna and atmosphere corrections are included; emission angle, roughness and tilt are not corrected.

entries.subject: Akatsuki IR2 2.26 micrometre night-side clouds
entries.finding: No full-coverage date sequence was qualified here; this surface emissivity addition retains the existing ultraviolet cloud data.
entries.revisitWhen: A particular Level 3 release and its usable geographic coverage are selected.

entries.subject: VIRTIS 1 micrometre surface emissivity
entries.finding: A calibrated geographic product and its southern coverage have not been qualified for this release. It is distinct from the Magellan microwave lens.

entries.subject: Native numeric USGS products and compact display grids
entries.finding: Numeric Magellan GTDR, reflectivity and roughness; emissivity keeps the identity, palette and calibration introduced by #828. Roughness uses the PDS formula because the detached ISIS multiplier conflicts.
